chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Abū ʿAlī Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Muṭahhar, who said:
I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام: I gave one hundred and fifty dīnārs to six persons so that they might perform hajj with it.

Then they returned, and some of them had not departed. Some came to me and mentioned that they had spent some of the dīnārs and that some remained, and that they would return to me what remained. I had intended to demand back what I had given to those who did not come to me.

So he عليه السلام wrote: “Do not pursue the one who did not come to you, and do not take anything from the one who came to you of what he brings back to you, and the reward has already become due from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.الدَّنَانِيرِ: the dinars; the funds some of them partially spent
key_terms.الْأَجْرُ: the reward; the recompense with Allah for the act
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: dinar; the monetary unit given for the delegated hajj
key_terms.لَا تَأْخُذْ: do not take; an instruction not to accept returned funds
key_terms.لَا تَتَعَرَّضْ: do not pursue or confront; an instruction not to go after them
key_terms.لِيَحُجُّوا: so that they may perform hajj on the giver’s behalf or by his funding
key_terms.يَرُدُّ: to return back; referring to the remaining money

ai.seo_question: If I gave money to others to perform hajj and they did not complete it, can I reclaim the money?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a case of delegated hajj in which money was given to several people, but some did not complete the journey and some wished to return leftover funds. Imam Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام instructs the questioner not to demand repayment or accept returned amounts, affirming that the spiritual reward is with Allah عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ. The report reflects legal and ethical guidance concerning expenditure for acts of worship and reliance upon divine recompense.
